items.title: 18.7.2 Ligand Exchange Reactions of Cobalt(II) Complexes

source_refs.note: Topic 18.7.2 with Figures 18.9 and 18.10, printed pages 25-26.

blocks.text: Cobalt(II) salts also form complex ions in aqueous solution. As mentioned in the case of copper(II), a Co²⁺(aq) ion refers to the complex ion [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺. This ion gives a pink colour to the aqueous solution of cobalt(II) sulphate. On adding sodium hydroxide solution, we see a blue precipitate of cobalt(II) hydroxide, which may turn pink on standing.

When excess ammonia solution is added to the cobalt(II) hydroxide precipitate, a ligand exchange reaction takes place. The ammonia ligands replace the water and hydroxide ligands, forming a soluble ammine complex, hexaamminecobalt(II) ions. The colour of the solution turns yellow (Figure 18.9).

blocks.alt: Four test tubes left to right: pink solution of [Co(H2O)6]2+; after NaOH solution, a blue precipitate of [Co(H2O)4(OH)2]; on standing, a pink precipitate; with an excess of ammonia, a yellow-brown solution of [Co(NH3)6]2+.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.9: Colour changes in [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ on addition of hydroxide and NH₃ (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.9).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 18.9 gives the last complex as [Co(NH₃)₆]² (the + sign is missing); the ion is [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺, as drawn above.
Water ligands in [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ can also be exchanged directly with ammonia ligands by adding concentrated ammonia solution.

The addition of concentrated hydrochloric acid drop by drop to an aqueous solution of cobalt(II) ions results in the formation of a blue solution containing the tetrahedral complex [CoCl₄]²⁻(aq) (Figure 18.10).

blocks.alt: Two test tubes: a pink solution of [Co(H2O)6]2+ turns into a blue solution of [CoCl4]2- on adding conc. HCl.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.10: Exchange of water molecules by chloride ions in a Co(II) complex (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.10).

blocks.text: Aqueous cobalt(II) ions usually form tetrahedral complexes with monodentate anionic ligands such as Cl⁻, OH⁻ and SCN⁻.
